title: Agent role manifest
description: The host-independent declaration of one agent in this architecture. This is the single source of truth for the agent's model tier, reasoning strength, tool grant, and mutation class; every host agent file is generated from it by scripts/render_agents.py. Prose lives in references/agents/<id>.md and is never duplicated here.

id.description: Agent name as hosts see it. Lowercase and hyphens only, because Claude Code and Cursor both derive the invocation name from it.

kind.description: What this manifest is FOR, which is not the same question as which position it fills. A worker is dispatched and returns a contract. The orchestrator dispatches workers, judges what they return, and talks to root through the mailbox. Root is dispatched by nobody: it runs as the main thread, holds the operator channel, and dispatches only the orchestrator. That last difference is not cosmetic - every derivation in this repository that reasons about delegation asks whether the role is itself dispatched, because a dispatched agent that delegates needs NESTED delegation and a main-thread one does not.

role.description: Which position this manifest fills. The three worker positions are a fixed three-agent loop, not an extensible registry: exactly one manifest each, and so is the orchestrator, and so is root. `kind` is what keeps that invariant enforceable now that manifests exist which are not workers.

description.description: Host-facing trigger description. Must say what the role returns and that it is dispatched by root, so nothing invokes it as a general-purpose helper.

mutation.description: Portable capability class, and the thing hosts disagree about most. 'read-only' means no shell and no write tools. 'read-and-run' means a shell exists solely to rerun named acceptance commands. 'write-scoped' means edits are permitted, but only inside the brief's write paths — a boundary no host enforces, so a write-scoped role always carries an unenforced disclosure.

model.description: Cheapest-viable tier plus the ordered escalation path. Never 'inherit': every host defaults to inheriting the parent, which silently makes a cheap worker as expensive as root.

escalation.description: Ordered, strictly increasing tiers. Root advances exactly one step per recorded failure, never on a hunch.

reasoning.description: Reasoning strength. Expressed portably here; rendered into whatever each host actually supports, or disclosed as unenforced where it supports nothing.

tools.description: Portable tool intent. 'allow' is the complete grant; 'deny' is belt-and-braces for hosts that support a denylist, and documentation everywhere else.

allow.description: The full grant. An empty shell grant is expressed by omitting 'run-commands', not by granting it and asking the agent not to use it.

shell_purpose.description: Required by scripts/validate_roles.py whenever 'run-commands' is in 'allow'. Naming the single reason a shell exists is what stops it becoming a general grant.

must_not.description: Prohibitions the role carries. Entries that hooks/ can enforce mechanically are enforced; the rest are rendered into the agent's own instructions and into the enforcement disclosure. `interfere-with-dispatch` is root's: hooks/root_write_guard.py refuses a root write inside an open dispatch's write paths, so the manifest and the shipped guard must agree about it.

returns.description: The contract this agent must return, as a single fenced JSON block. Root validates a worker's or the orchestrator's return with scripts/check_return.py before acting on it. Root itself returns `none`: it answers to the operator in prose, and there is nobody above it to validate a schema.

prose.description: Path to the canonical role prose. Host agent files point at it rather than restating it, so the role text exists in exactly one place.

launch.description: How this agent is started, and what it may start. Present only on a root manifest - every other agent in this architecture is dispatched, and a dispatched agent has no launch of its own to declare. scripts/validate_roles.py refuses it elsewhere; the schema cannot, having no `not`.

main_thread.description: Root runs as the main thread and only as the main thread. It is a constant rather than a boolean because there is no other value this architecture supports: the type restriction root's isolation rests on binds only for a main-thread agent, so a root launched any other way is a root whose boundary is not in force. See ADR 0003 D10.

delegates_to.description: The role ids root may dispatch, by `role` rather than by `id`. Rendered into the host's own scoping syntax where it has one, and disclosed as unenforced where it does not. Every entry must name a role manifest that exists, which is what stops this drifting into a list of agents nobody ships.

initial_prompt.description: Submitted automatically when root starts, on hosts that support it. This is where the startup capability check of ADR 0003 D11 is triggered: a check root has to remember to run is a check that does not run on the session where it matters.

modelTier.description: Vendor-neutral tier. hosts/<host>.json maps each tier to that host's own model id, so a role manifest never names a vendor model.

effort.description: Reasoning strength, in Claude Code's vocabulary because it is the most granular of the supported hosts. hosts/<host>.json maps these onto coarser scales, and declares when a host can express none of them.

toolIntent.description: Portable intent, not a host tool name. hosts/<host>.json maps each intent to concrete tool names; an intent a host cannot express is a rendering error, not a silent drop.
